rules.when: Data missing or unusable, or a layer wasn't checked
rules.to: a person, with one line saying what's missing

rules.when: A camera or the joint stream froze and came back within 1 s
rules.to: the robot: restart the stream, hold, retry

rules.when: A camera froze for longer, or 3 or more times
A joint stopped following and caught up within 1 s
A joint stopped following, sat pinned, is miscalibrated, or the leader's angle wrapped
3 or more impossible one frame jumps on one motor
A stall or missed grasps with fresh pictures and joints that followed
Two causes too close to call, a standing fault on the arm, or contact versus a dead joint
One missed grasp then a good one, or one bad bus read

checks.name: Camera froze
checks.signal: Picture change between consecutive frames (80x60 gray) while the joints that move or are seen by that camera are moving
checks.threshold: change under 0.51 gray levels for 3+ frames while arm motion is over 2% of range per frame
checks.why: A still scene and a frozen camera look the same in the image alone; the joints are what separate a dead sensor from a quiet room. The change level was calibrated on injected freezes through LeRobot's own video compression.

checks.name: Joint stream repeated
checks.signal: Every arm joint reads bit identical while the lag corrected command is moving
checks.threshold: 3+ identical frames while the command moves
checks.why: One joint going flat is an actuator. All of them going flat at once is the data path: a cached bus read or duplicated rows.

checks.name: Camera runs late
checks.signal: Delay at which picture change lines up best with arm motion
checks.threshold: judged per arm as a median over runs; flagged at 3 frames (100 ms) or more
checks.why: A single run's estimate moves by a frame, so it is never used against one run.

checks.name: Joint not following its command
checks.signal: Gap between the follower's position and its command from a few frames earlier, after removing the arm's own calibration fit
checks.threshold: gap over 15% of range for 0.4 s; under 1.0 s and caught up means the robot cleared it
checks.why: Healthy followers stay under 7% at the 99th percentile. A limp or stalled servo passes 15% within a few hundred ms. The mode (stalled, sagging, lagging, held) comes from how far command and follower each travelled.

checks.name: Offset at rest
checks.signal: Median follower minus leader during pauses
checks.threshold: over 5% of range in the same direction in 80% of pauses
checks.why: A reseated horn or a stale calibration file. A policy learns to compensate until it can't, which looks like a worse model.

checks.name: Calibration mismatch
checks.signal: Slope of follower against leader over all of the arm's data
checks.threshold: slope off by more than 15% on a joint that moved over a quarter of the arm's span
checks.why: Leader and follower are calibrated separately, so their readings can disagree by a gain. Reported once per arm, not as repeated tracking loss.

checks.name: Bad bus reads
checks.signal: One frame jump in a joint reading that comes straight back
checks.threshold: jump over 25% of range returning within 3 frames; 3 on one motor is a ticket
checks.why: An STS3215 can't move a quarter of its range in 33 ms. One is logged; three on the same motor is a harness or bus problem.

checks.name: Leader angle wrap
checks.signal: One frame command jump that stays
checks.threshold: over 50% of range in one frame, not returning
checks.why: The leader's reading wrapping past +-180 degrees sends the follower the long way round. This is the cause; the tracking loss that follows is the symptom.

checks.name: Pinned at a limit
checks.signal: Follower at the edge of its observed range while the command pushes further and keeps moving
checks.threshold: within 1% of the extreme, command 5% past it for 0.5 s
checks.why: A joint limit or a calibration range that is too narrow.

checks.name: Stall
checks.signal: Command and position still on every joint
checks.threshold: for 2.0 s or more, ignoring the first and last 1.5 s of a run
checks.why: The trigger deployed home robots use to call for help: the robot stalls for some time. Measured from motion, so the onset is when the robot stopped, not when anyone noticed.

checks.name: Missed grasps in a row
checks.signal: After each close command, how far short of the command the gripper stopped
checks.threshold: within 3% of range is an empty close; 5% or more short is holding something; 2 or more empties in a row with nothing held between is a sequence
checks.why: A metric home robot fleets publish. One empty close followed by a good grasp is the robot clearing its own miss.

plain.sensing.stale_camera.wrist camera: wrist camera froze while the arm moved
plain.sensing.stale_camera.fixed camera: scene camera froze while the arm moved
plain.sensing.stale_state.joint_stream: joint stream repeated while commanded to move
plain.actuation.rest_offset: follower sits offset from its leader at rest
plain.actuation.gain_mismatch: follower and leader calibrated over different spans
plain.actuation.not_tracking: follower doesn't track its leader on a joint
plain.actuation.bus_glitch: impossible one frame jumps on a motor
plain.actuation.pinned: joint pinned at its limit while pushed further
plain.actuation.command_wrap: leader reading wrapped past its end
plain.task.stall: stopped making progress for 2 s or more
plain.task.missed_grasp_sequence: 2 or more missed grasps in a row
plain.integrity.frame_count: video and joint row counts disagree
